name: What unit mix works best for apartment construction in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: How do studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom units affect feasibility and rent potential in LA apartment projects?
mainEntity.text: How do studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom units affect feasibility and rent potential in LA apartment projects?

acceptedAnswer.text: The right unit mix is a major feasibility driver in Los Angeles apartment construction. Smaller units such as studios and one-bedrooms can improve density and sometimes maximize rent per square foot, which helps on tight sites. Larger one- and two-bedroom units may appeal to different renter segments and can support stronger long-term occupancy, but they also reduce total unit count and may require more space per apartment. The best mix depends on the neighborhood, parking strategy, lot size, and target market. In a dense infill area, compact layouts may make the project pencil better. In a family-oriented or higher-end submarket, larger units may align better with demand. A good concept plan should test different mixes before final design so the owner can see how unit count, layout efficiency, and rental performance interact. The most profitable mix is often the one that balances density with livability and code compliance.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best unit mix depends on the site, parking, and target renter profile. Smaller units can increase density and improve rent per square foot, while larger units may attract longer-term tenants and families but reduce total unit count on constrained lots.
